correctness.rationale: The complete polytope vertex classification follows from total unimodularity and connected tight-edge graphs. Exact rational orbit feasibility maxima and positive log-determinant KKT weights establish the nonspherical cases p=2..5. An equilateral-ball lower bound and a global squared-norm bound 2 on every exceptional vertex establish the spherical regime p>=6, including the strict contact change at p=7. The standalone checker independently reruns all finite certificates; the infinite claim is proved algebraically, not extrapolated.

originality.rationale: The claim is a complete minimum-volume enclosing ellipsoid of the Lipschitz DUAL potential unit ball for all complete unit-edge graphs with one deleted edge. A dual John ellipsoid, or a PRIMAL Löwner ellipsoid, answers the polar opposite problem and cannot imply this one by naming alone. Published general minimum-volume ellipsoid optimization supplies the method but not the sharp p=6 sphere transition and p=7 contact transition. No matching statement or dominating theorem was found in accessible searches, but unindexed equivalent graph-specific results remain possible.
residual_risks: Full text of some close graph-specific indexed reports could not be read at the supplied links; their detailed appendices remain a possible source of equivalent or stronger results.
A general optimal-design theorem may admit a prior explicit specialization not identified by the present searches.
This is a self-review, not an independent scientific audit.

value.rationale: The exterior minimal-volume ellipsoid is a canonical affine-geometric invariant once the zero-sum Euclidean structure is fixed. The exact four nonround ellipsoids, sharp dimension-8 spherical onset, and dimension-9 disappearance of novel vertex contacts constitute a motivated, all-dimensional phase classification. The invariance despite strict enlargement of the underlying norm ball is a substantive structural transition, not a renamed scalar or routine finite computation.
